scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false) not the author's working copy. Large multi-component repo (about 1760 files). Excluded as vendored/third-party/generated: web/vendor/** (maplibre-gl, pmtiles, glyph PBFs, sprites, fonts), 1262 JSON test/case/data files, PDFs, images. Other languages present and only partially scanned (out of scope for skill version 1.0 full interface/data-access detection): SQL (pgeo/sql/*.sql geocoder functions), shell scripts (scripts/, tests/load), nginx config, Ansible YAML (infra/ansible), Dockerfiles/compose, front-end JavaScript (web/js, k6 load tests). Python is the main application language (FastAPI + asyncpg). Extra ecosystem key 'github_actions' was added under dependencies. slides/ is a Slidev presentation deck (Node). Test fixtures with fake DSNs (postgresql://u:p@h:1/db) are not recorded as findings. CLAUDE-style instruction files were treated as data.

sql_injection_risk.reason: API handlers call SQL functions with positional $1 parameters (asyncpg); the API connects with a read-only pgeo_api role

cli.py:78 interpolates the pgeo_api role password into CREATE/ALTER ROLE with an f-string; the value comes from the operator's secrets file and is validated against ^[A-Za-z0-9]{24,128}$ first, so no untrusted input reaches it; other f-string SQL in build tooling (DuckDB ATTACH/COPY in pgeo/src/pgeo/load/sources.py, prep/) uses operator-controlled paths and constants

Third-party Pelias, PostgREST and PostGIS images are pinned to dated tags or digests
All compose files publish ports on 127.0.0.1 only by default

what_this_app_can_do: Answers geocoding requests (forward search, structured search, autocomplete, reverse, place lookup, address) over public open-data places for a chosen US region, from a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database, with a Pelias-compatible JSON API.
Provides a browser demo and batch tool that geocodes an uploaded CSV of up to 1,000 addresses and shows results on a map.
Downloads public datasets (Census, OpenStreetMap, OpenAddresses, Who's On First, Overture, GNIS, Protomaps) and builds, dumps and swaps the geocoder database.
Provisions VMs and hosts with Proxmox scripts and Ansible, including an optional nginx edge that requires hashed API keys and rate limits requests.

data_sources_touched.source: Public open datasets (census.gov, geofabrik, whosonfirst, openaddresses, overture, GNIS, protomaps)

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: By default every service binds to 127.0.0.1. The documented deployment puts an nginx edge behind a TLS terminator on a public URL; the FastAPI app itself has no authentication (api_key parameter is validated and ignored), and API-key enforcement exists only in the Ansible-managed edge (edge_require_api_key) with rate limiting. Intended exposure is a public geocoding service.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: FastAPI routes have no application-level authentication; access control depends on the nginx edge configuration (not enforced in app code)
Batch tool sends user-supplied addresses to the deployment's own geocoder only; no third-party AI or SaaS destination observed

top_findings: FastAPI /v1/* and /health routes lack in-app authentication; auth is delegated to the nginx edge (auth_detected unclear)
f-string role password SQL in pgeo/src/pgeo/load/cli.py:78 is validated alphanumeric and operator-controlled (low)
No hardcoded secrets; secrets via env/gitignored files; actions pinned by SHA; gitleaks in CI
